transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. It's a bit difficult for me to admit, but I keep trying to get rid of what I eat after I overdo it, and I feel like I can't stop doing it on my own.
After these episodes of overeating, do you typically use self-induced vomiting or laxatives to compensate, or do you instead use periods of fasting or excessive exercise?

I make myself throw up after I overeat, and I usually turn on the bathroom fan so my husband won't hear me because I feel so ashamed. It feels like the only way to erase the calories and calm my panic, but I don't use laxatives, fast, or do any excessive exercise.
During these episodes where you feel you cannot stop eating, do you feel a sense of loss of control, such as feeling like you cannot stop or are unable to control what or how much you are eating?

Yes, absolutely. It feels like a switch flips and I just can't stop, even when I'm telling myself to put the food down. My hands just keep reaching for more until I'm uncomfortably stuffed, and it honestly feels like I'm in some kind of trance.
How many times a week, on average, do these episodes of overeating and subsequent vomiting occur, and for how long has this pattern been happening?

This cycle has been going on for about seven months now, starting around the time my husband's heart condition got worse and my doctor really pressured me about my weight. It usually happens about once or twice a week, almost always on those really difficult, exhausting days of taking care of him.
